newsitem.title: UK: Dorrell set to quit Tory leadership race -- BBC.
newsitem.headline: Dorrell set to quit Tory leadership race -- BBC.

text.p: Former health secretary Stephen Dorrell looks certain to pull out of the race for the leadership of the British Conservative Party and give his support to former finance minister Kenneth Clarke, the BBC said
The BBC said there was speculation that Dorrell would be given the role of Clarke's deputy if he won the election in which voting begins on June 10.

The BBC said Dorrell was thought to have secured no more than nine supporters among the 165 Conservative members of parliament left in the House of Commons after the Labour Party's landslide May 1 election defeat.

There are four other candidates to succeed former prime minister John Major as Conservative Party leader: former Welsh Secretary William Hague, arch-anti-European John Redwood, former home secretary Michael Howard and former social security secretary Peter Lilley. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7947
